Wheat is a group of wild and domesticated grasses of the genus Triticum ( / ˈ t r ɪ t ɪ k ə m / ). [ 3 ] As cereals , they are cultivated for their grains , which are staple foods around the world. Well-known wheat species and hybrids include the most widely grown common wheat ( T. aestivum ), spelt , durum , emmer , einkorn , and Khorasan or Kamut . The archaeological record suggests that wheat was first cultivated in the regions of the Fertile Crescent around 9600 BC.
